Definition: Pisgah, a Mountain East of Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Pisgah is the mountain east of Jordan from which Moses saw the land he would not enter. God told him to climb to the top of Pisgah and look in every direction in Deuteronomy 3:27, and Moses went up to the top of Pisgah in Deuteronomy 34:1 and saw all the land of Gilead. Balak brought Balaam to the top of Pisgah too, in Numbers 23:14, hoping for a curse.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Pisgah is the mountain of seeing without entering — Moses saw the promise fulfilled for others, and trusted God with what he never touched.
